summary: I worked on the frontend of WebManza, a drag-and-drop builder that lets merchants set up an online store without code. Besides the builder, I set up the WebManza blog and portfolio site and a merchant sign-up landing page for a partner campaign.

projects.title: WebManza Store Builder
projects.what: A drag-and-drop e-commerce builder where merchants assemble a storefront from ready-made sections. I worked on the Next.js frontend of the builder and the stores it produces.
built: Worked on the storefront section library: banners, parallax heroes, category grids, product sliders, testimonials, blog and service blocks.
Moved storefront pages to server-side rendering in Next.js so search engines could index store content.
Moved data fetching to Redux RTK Query so repeated requests were cached instead of sent again.
Built data hooks for products and campaign products used by the storefront sections.

projects.title: WebManza Blog and Portfolio Site
projects.what: WebManza needed a blog and portfolio site. I built it on top of the store builder's section library so it shared the same look and components.
built: Set up the project from the storefront codebase and removed everything not needed for a blog.
Built blog listing and detail layouts with a mobile sidebar and a table layout for posts.
Built a hero handler for blog pages and a new team card that supports four-column grids.
Added fade and hover animations for blog cards and tuned slider settings.
Fixed mobile issues with images inside text blocks and social share icons.

projects.title: Merchant Sign-up Landing Page
projects.what: A landing page for a partner campaign that invited merchants to open a WebManza store, with pricing, FAQ, merchant agreement and a get-started flow.
built: Set up the Next.js App Router project for the landing page.
Included pages for about, pricing, FAQ, privacy policy and merchant agreement.
Included a contact API route that sends enquiries by email.
